messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for model-runtime pool 'us-west-2' (model: llama-13b-int8). anomaly score 0.83. auto-page to #incidents and @marta @oncall-sre

marta: seeing it. dashboards show spike in 5xx and timeouts starting ~2001234400. overall 5xx ~11% on the gateway for the pool. routing fallback kicking but still saturated.

raj: attaching sample runtime logs from one host:
```
[2026-03-12T15:03:45Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: seq_len=2048 -> alloc KVCache 1.2G
[2026-03-12T15:03:46Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: ERROR: segfault at 0x0 (signal 11)
[2026-03-12T15:03:46Z] kernel: OOM killer invoked: task model-runner pid=4123
```

sam: this smells like large sequence paths exhausting GPU memory + occasional segfaults. we're getting both OOM kills and 5xx from the gateway when runners crash.

emily: confirmed customer impact: ~14% of API calls to hosted endpoints backed by that pool returning 5xx/timeouts. top affected customers: 3 high-traffic PLG apps (we'll notify).

marta: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) remove longest-prefix-heavy traffic by enabling `max_input_tokens=1024` on the gateway for this pool; 2) scale up hot spares (add 4 nodes of p4d) if quota; 3) enable routing fallback to quantized smaller variant `llama-13b-q4` for new requests. any objections?

raj: doing (3) now: updating routing policy in feature-gateway -> policy id 0x9a to prefer q4 when runtime health < 0.8.

platform-sre: starting canary restart of model-runner on 3 nodes: `kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/model-runner --selector=pool=us-west-2 --grace-period=30`

sam: while restarts go, recommend we turn on a short-circuit to return 429 for extremely long prompts to reduce tail pressure. i'll push that patch to gateway: `PATCH /config/pools/us-west-2`

marta: agreed. also enable extra logging on any segfault to capture host / driver stack: `ENV RUNTIME_CRASH_DUMP=1` on the pods. raj can you patch the daemonset?

raj: patching now. also toggled `enable_kv_limit=true` to force eviction for seq_len > 1536 for the affected model.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-3284. Severity: Sev2. Links: runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-runtime-crash, pagerduty -> https://pd/INC-3284

emily: customer comms draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting inference in US-West. Workarounds: retry with smaller inputs or pin to dedicated pools. We'll update hourly." any edits?

marta: good. add note that we have a mitigation (fallback to q4) active and that we expect degraded latency for a subset of requests.

platform-sre: restarts completed on canary nodes; logs show SIGSEGV on two older GPU hosts with driver 535.x. we should cordon those nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 gpu-node-43` and drain after evicting critical pods.

sam: adding temporary routing rule to exclude those hosts from pool allocation. done.

raj: we've enabled fallback routing and reduced `max_input_tokens` at gateway; new 5xx rate dropped to ~3.2% in 8m. latency increased ~80ms p50.

marta: great. next steps: 1) cordon and repro on isolated host to capture coredump, 2) engage infra to upgrade driver on affected amber hosts, 3) follow up with customers with ETA. who's owner for driver upgrade?

platform-sre: i'll own driver upgrade. ETA 4 hours to patch rolling nodes (staggered). will coordinate maintenance window; we can speed up if customers demand.

emily: notifying customer success and sending the updated comms now. tagging top 3 customers and support for priority tickets.

marta: note for postmortem: capture sequence length distribution, KV cache growth, and any differences between q4/q8 builds that mask the bug. also check if quantization path avoids segfault (it seems so).

raj: capturing debug artifacts: kernel logs, coredumps uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/INC-3284/, link: https://s3.redwood/INC-3284/dumps

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigation in place -> fallback routing + gateway rate-limit. 5xx reduced to 3.1%. Incident status: Mitigated.

marta: switching to monitoring mode. keep this thread for driver upgrade and postmortem notes. once driver roll is done and hosts stable for 24h we can resolve.

sam: quick reminder: if we need to permanently avoid this class of segfaults, schedule a hard limit on seq_len at the API layer and document in model profiles.

emily: acknowledged. I'll prepare stakeholder update and include impact numbers + timeline.

platform-sre: started rolling driver upgrade on a subset. will report progress here.

marta: thanks all. good triage and fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
